page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3 register in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests, consistently achieve average tier results. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also perform in the middle 50%, though the overall Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g5.6xlarge offers a balanced resource density for workloads that can leverage parallel processing to offset its modest single-core speeds. It is suitable for multi-threaded general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, Redis database operations, and moderate software compilation. It can also handle small to medium language model inference tasks, though it is not configured for large-scale AI or storage-heavy database deployments due to the absence of local NVMe SSDs and GPU accelerators.
